texts: Wake, O sleeper! The net of death is already closing, and the chance is slipping through its mesh
My doctor called this morning and said the results cannot wait, and for the first time I am lying awake thinking I have spent forty years asleep with a net around me
need a doha that shouts wake up before the net of death closes on you
Write a doha with a loud, urgent voice telling the sleeping person to get up now, because the net of death is spread and once it closes there will be no second chance to do what matters
net, wake up now
Wake up, the moth is already circling the flame, and soon the wings will burn and the chance will be lost
moth, wake now
doha with a moth, warning me to wake up before it is too late
Please write a doha in an urgent tone where a moth flies closer and closer to the flame and the voice shouts at the listener to wake up now, before death arrives and the chance is lost for ever
My friend kept saying next year he would change his life, and then a heart attack took him at forty-one; I keep thinking of him circling and circling like a moth, and I do not want to be next
doha with a mirror and tongue, wake up now before death comes
Write a doha in which a person looks in the mirror and sees a face already tired, and his own tongue shouts at him to wake up now before death takes the chance he keeps postponing
I looked in the mirror this morning, saw my father's tired face, and my own tongue said you are running out of days to fix things, get up now
The mirror shows a face that will not last, and the tongue cries out: wake, before the face is gone and the chance with it
mirror, tongue, wake up
Give me an urgent doha telling the sleeper to wake before the potter and clay are done and the mosque is closed, because death is on the road and little time is left
The call from the mosque woke me at dawn, and a young man was being buried nearby; I lay shaking, thinking I have slept all my life and the potter and clay of my days are almost spent
doha with a potter and clay and a mosque, wake up before death arrives
potter and clay, mosque, wake
The potter and clay are quiet, the mosque calls loudly, and death is on the road: rise, O sleeper, rise now
wake up, death is near
I got a message that my college friend collapsed at the gym and did not make it, and I have been staring at the ceiling since; I know I have been wasting my days and I must start now
Kabir shouted at people who sleep through their lives, so please write a doha in his urgent voice, telling the listener to wake up now before death comes and the time is lost beyond recall
doha that screams at me to wake up before death comes
Wake, wake! The messenger of death is at the gate, and your sleep has stolen the hours you swore to use
Please write a doha in which an urgent voice calls to a swan floating asleep on the water, warning that death comes in the dark and the chance to wake and do the right thing will be lost for ever
doha with a swan, telling someone to wake up before it is too late
swan, wake up now
Wake up, white swan, the evening is falling on the pond and the night of death does not wait for your plans

My father floated through life like a swan, calm and untroubled, and the doctors told us last week that there are very few days left; I want a doha that shakes people awake before this happens to them
doha with a churn, wake up before death comes and its too late
churn, wake up now
Write a doha in an urgent voice that tells the sleeping person to get up and churn the butter now, before death arrives, because there will be no churning once the hour has passed
My mother got up at four to churn the butter every day, and my brother who sleeps till noon was told just this week by the doctor that his lungs are failing; I want a doha that wakes him
Rise and work the churn this very hour, for death is walking up the lane and the cream will not wait
Wake now, O heedless one, and churn the milk of your days, for death stands near and the butter will not wait
Write a doha in which a voice urgently shouts at a person to wake from sleep and to churn the milk of his life into butter, before death carries him away with the milk still unchurned
My grandmother kept shouting at me to get up, drink my milk and work the churn before the day was gone, and now she is gone, and I realise she was telling me something more urgent
milk, churn, wake up
doha with milk and a churn, wake up before death comes, urgent
At the festival a decorated elephant was led past an old man with a pearl who slept on his cot, and my guru said, that is the world, asleep while death walks by; wake the people
elephant, pearl, wake up now
doha with an elephant and a pearl, wake up before it is too late, urgent
Write a doha with an elephant and a pearl in an urgent voice, telling the sleeper the elephant's tread is the tread of death, and the pearl he sleeps on cannot buy another hour
The elephant of death is walking toward the sleeping man with a pearl in his fist, and the voice cries: wake, wake
Tell the priest asleep over his books in an urgent doha to wake up, because the ocean of the world is wide and death is a storm that will not wait for his sermon to finish
doha with a priest and an ocean, wake up before death comes
Our priest has been preaching the same sermon for forty years, and last week, as the ocean wind rose, he slept through the evening prayer; I want a doha to shake all such sleepers awake
O priest, the ocean is rising and the tide of death does not read sermons: wake and cross while the shore is near
priest, ocean, wake up now
seed, wake up now
Wake, the seed lies unplanted and the season is closing; death does not wait for those who sleep through spring
Please write a doha in an urgent voice telling someone to plant the seed of good deeds right now, because the season is nearly over, death is near, and the field will not be sown again
I found a packet of seed my father meant to sow before he died, and it is still unopened in his drawer; I know I am doing the same with my own life and I must wake up
doha with a seed, wake up and do something before death arrives
market, wake up now
Write a doha in an urgent voice telling the sleeper in the market that the day is ending, the sellers are packing up, and death will close the gates before he has bought the one thing that matters
I wasted another Sunday in the market buying things I do not need, and then the news of my cousin's death arrived; I want a doha that shakes me awake
doha with a market, wake up before death comes
The market bustles while death stands at the edge of the street, and the voice cries: wake, before the last stall is shut
doha with a washerman and a traveler, wake up before death comes
Write a doha in an urgent voice, where a washerman at the water's edge shouts to a traveler dozing nearby to wake and wash the dirt from his heart before death arrives and the chance is gone
washerman, traveler, wake up
The washerman cries to the dozing traveler: wake, there is dirt to wash and death is walking down the road
A washerman shouted at a traveler who had fallen asleep by the road, and I thought he was shouting at me; I have been asleep too long, and the road is almost over
swan, wake up
doha with a swan, wake up before death, urgent please
Write an urgent doha that tells the sleeper to wake and become a swan who sorts the true from the false before the dark of death falls and the chance to choose is gone
I kept putting off the one big decision of my life, and then my father collapsed, and as I sat beside the pond I thought of a swan that keeps moving while I sleep; wake up, I told myself
Awake, white swan, the lake is darkening and death will not wait for your drowsy dream to end
I realised yesterday that I have not once used my pearl necklace nor my cotton quilt for anything that matters, and my aunt's funeral last week made me scream inside: wake up now
The pearl sleeps in its box and the cotton quilt in its chest, and death comes quietly: wake up, the hour is nearly spent
doha with a pearl and cotton, wake up before death arrives

Write a doha in an urgent voice telling someone sleeping under a cotton quilt with a pearl in his pocket to wake now, because death is near and neither the pearl nor the quilt will give him another day
pearl, cotton, wake up
doha about the sun rising and telling a sleeper to wake up before death
The sun was high when I finally woke up today, and my phone had a message that my cousin passed in the night; I don't want to sleep through another day
Write a doha in an urgent voice saying the sun has risen and the sleeper is still in bed, though death walks in daylight too, and every hour wasted is an hour that will never be given back
The sun is up and you are asleep, and death needs no sunrise to find you: rise, rise now
sun, wake up now
The bee hums in the garden and knows the flowers will fade, while you sleep, O heedless one: wake before death
Please write a doha in an urgent voice telling a sleeping person to wake up like a bee that gathers honey all day because the flowers are fading, and death will not wait for him to begin
bee, wake up now
My neighbour keeps a bee hive and works from dawn, and I envied him, then I heard that his friend died in his sleep last night; wake me up, someone, I have wasted so much time
doha with a bee, wake up before death comes
Write a doha in which a voice cries to someone who is sleeping on the sand as the day runs out, that death is walking toward him across the dunes, and he must wake and use these last hours
sand, wake up
doha with sand, wake up before death comes
The sand runs through your fingers as you sleep: wake, O fool, for death does not leave footprints before it arrives
I stood on the dunes watching the wind take my footprints in the sand, and a phone call told me that my teacher had died; I woke up inside, and I want a doha that wakes others too
Please write a doha in which the voice shouts at a sleeping person to wake and see the cage of his body open and the bier waiting, because death comes quickly and the chance to act is lost
Last week I saw a bird leave its open cage and a bier pass on the same street, and I woke that night in a sweat; I want a doha that does for everyone what that night did for me
The cage is opening and the bier is waiting: rise, O sleeper, the hour of leaving is near
cage, bier, wake up
doha with a cage and a bier, wake up now before death
The blind man at our street corner holds his rope and walks straight every morning, while I with my two eyes sleep through the day; I felt ashamed and want a doha that wakes me up
blind man, rope, wake now
Write a doha in an urgent voice that tells a blind man to hold the rope and climb before death cuts it, and says that the one who is sleeping with open eyes is blinder still and must wake now
The blind man grips the rope and climbs, while the one with open eyes sleeps on: wake, wake, for death is near
doha with a blind man and a rope, wake up before death comes
moon, wake up now
Write a doha in an urgent voice that tells someone to wake while the moon is still up, since the night is nearly over and the dawn of death will not give another night to do the work of life
The moon is sinking and you are still dreaming, and death is the dawn that comes for those who sleep through the night
doha with the moon, wake up before death comes
I sat up with the moon through the night after my uncle's funeral, thinking how many nights I have slept through without a thought; I want a doha to shake others before they wake like this
My brother has been postponing his life for twenty years, and today he was told his illness may not wait; I want a doha that screams wake up while there is time
doha that screams wake up before death comes, short and urgent please
Kabir shouted at the people of his day to stop sleeping through their lives, so write a doha in the same urgent voice, telling the reader that death is coming and the opportunity will not return
wake up now
Wake, O sleeper, the hour is almost spent and death has come to the edge of your dream
Please write a doha in an urgent voice in which a cuckoo cries from the edge of the market, warning the busy crowd that death is near and that they have bought everything except what they needed
I spent another Sunday in the market without buying what I came for, and as the cuckoo called at dusk I realised my life is going the same way; I want a doha that shouts wake up
doha with a cuckoo and a market, wake up before death comes
cuckoo, market, wake up
The cuckoo calls above the market's noise, and its cry is: wake, buyers, for death is closing the gates
A leaf fell on my desk this morning in a meeting I did not care about, and I stood up, knowing my life was slipping away; I want a doha that wakes the others
doha with a leaf, wake up before death comes
Please write a doha in an urgent voice telling a sleeper that every falling leaf is a warning, that death is walking toward him through the autumn, and that he must wake now to do what he came for
A leaf falls from the branch of your days, and the wind of death is rising: wake, wake before the bough is bare
leaf, wake up now
washerman, wake up now
Give me an urgent doha in which a washerman beats the clothes and tells the listener to wake up and wash the dirt from his own heart before death arrives and the water is gone
doha with a washerman, wake up and wash your heart before death comes
Our washerman asked me why I sleep so late each day, and then added that his father died in his sleep; I haven't slept properly since and I want a doha for such sleepers
The washerman beats the clothes and calls: wake, O sleeper, wash your heart before the water of days runs dry
The tongue is silent, the grindstone turns, and death comes in the dust: wake, speak the truth while you can
Urge the sleeper in a doha to use his tongue and speak the Name while the grindstone of days still turns, because death will grind him down and the time to speak will be over
tongue, grindstone, wake up

My grandmother worked her grindstone until the very last day, and her tongue never stopped telling us to use our time; I now understand what she meant, and I want a doha that tells the rest of us the same
doha with a tongue and a grindstone, wake up before death comes
I have been thinking about my uncle who had everything planned and then was gone in one night, and I want a doha that tells me to stop sleeping and act while I can
wake up, death is coming
Wake, O drowsy soul, for the messenger of death is already on the road and he does not knock twice
doha that tells people to wake up right now before death takes them
Kabir cried out that those who sleep through life will wake to find death at their pillow, so write a doha in his urgent voice telling the heedless to wake up now, before the time to change is gone
From my rooftop I watched the stars fade at dawn and a siren go by with an ambulance, and I thought, you are asleep and the night is almost over; I want a doha for this
The stars go out one by one and you are still asleep: wake, for the dawn that follows is the dawn of death

Write a doha in an urgent voice that tells a sleeping person to wake up while the stars are still visible, because death is the dawn that follows, and nobody who sleeps through the night is ready for it
doha with stars, wake up before death comes
stars, wake up now
doha with a blind man, wake up before its too late
Please write a doha in an urgent voice that tells the one who sleeps in comfort like a blind man to open his eyes and see that death is coming and the chance to repent will be gone
blind man, wake up
The blind man cries for light and the sleeper has eyes and will not use them: wake, O sleeper, death is near
I noticed that the blind man who sells tickets near the station is awake more than I am in my life, and my friend's sudden death this week made me shake; I want a doha for this
Write an urgent doha telling the one who sleeps like a chakor bird gazing at a diamond to wake, because death is near and he has been staring at the wrong thing all his life
doha with a chakor bird and a diamond, wake up before death comes
chakor bird, diamond, wake up
My uncle kept staring at his collection of diamond jewellery and a chakor bird sculpture, and passed away last month without ever using his life; I want a doha to wake others
The chakor bird stares at the sky and the miser at his diamond, and death comes to both: wake, wake
pearl, wake up now
The pearl lies in the oyster of your days, and death comes for the sleeper who never opened it: wake, open it now
I found my mother's pearl earrings in a box and realised that she saved them for an occasion that never came, and then I realised I am doing the same with my life; wake me up
doha with a pearl, wake up before death comes
Write a doha in an urgent voice telling someone to wake and take out the pearl of this life before death snatches it away and he is left with nothing but regret and an empty box
needle, washerman, wake up
Write a doha in an urgent voice in which a washerman picks up a needle and tells the sleeper to stitch up his torn life before death arrives, because the fabric will not hold much longer
doha with a needle and a washerman, wake up now before death arrives
The needle is lost in the washerman's heap, and death is walking in: wake and mend what is torn
My tailor friend threads a needle in the dark and a washerman I know says the same, that you must mend your life before it tears, and then my friend died young; I want a doha that wakes people
My father tied a rope round the cattle every night, and I was too lazy to help; he is gone now and I want a doha that wakes the lazy before they regret it, with a rope and a palanquin
doha with a rope and a palanquin, wake up before death comes
Write a doha in an urgent voice in which the rope that ties the palanquin is fraying and the sleeper inside is told to wake up and get out before death carries him away, with no time to spare
rope, palanquin, wake up
The rope is frayed and the palanquin trembles, and the sleeper inside is told: wake, get out, death is near
Write a doha in an urgent voice in which a cage holds a sleeping bird and a pot of water stands empty beside it, and death is approaching, so the one who sleeps must wake and fill the pot now
doha with a cage and a pot of water, wake up before death comes
The pot of water is empty and the cage is closing: wake, O sleeper, death is at the gate
cage, pot of water, wake
My grandfather kept a bird in a cage with a pot of water beside it, forgot to fill it once, and the bird died; I feel like that bird now, and I want a doha that wakes me
doha with a net, wake up before death throws it
Write an urgent doha in which a fisherman casts a net over the sleeping swimmers, and the voice shouts to wake and swim free before the net closes and death takes them all
My uncle fishes with a net at night and said the swimmers never wake until they are caught; I realised I am one and I want a doha to wake all of us
net, wake up now
The net is cast over the sleeping water: wake and swim, O soul, while there is still room
The seed is waiting and the spinning wheel is turning, and death comes to the one who sleeps between them: wake, wake
Write an urgent doha telling a sleeper to wake up, plant the seed and spin his days before death comes and the spinning wheel falls silent for ever
My aunt spun at her spinning wheel and saved her seed for the next season, and she did not wake up one morning in the winter; I want a doha that wakes others before that happens
doha with a seed and a spinning wheel, wake up before death comes
seed, spinning wheel, wake up
O drowsy soul, the day of leaving is near, and the hour you wasted will never return: rise, rise
My friend's father promised every year that next year he would take a trip, and he died in March; I want a doha that wakes me from my own endless next year
Kabir cried that the sleeping soul will lose the chance to cross the world, so please write a doha in the same urgent voice telling the heedless to wake before death comes and the chance is gone
wake up now
doha that says wake up now, death is coming
Write a doha in an urgent voice that tells the sleeper to stop decorating his house and wake up, because death is already at the gate, and nothing he has built can answer when he is called
doha about a house, wake up and do the real work before death comes
You paint the walls of your house and death is painting your name on a different wall: wake, wake
house, wake up
My cousin spent years renovating his house and then collapsed on the stairs of it, with half the rooms unfinished; I want a doha that wakes people from that kind of sleep
A moth flew round my grandmother as she lay, and as the forehead mark on her brow faded, I realised how I have been wasting the days she gave me; wake up, I told myself
doha with a forehead mark and a moth, wake up before death comes
Write a doha in an urgent voice in which a moth circles a flame and a person with a forehead mark sleeps in prayer without meaning it, and the voice tells him to wake now before death comes
forehead mark, moth, wake
The moth leaps toward the flame and the forehead mark is only paint: wake, wake, for death is real
death is near
My colleague jumped up at the news of an accident down the road and went quiet for the rest of the day, saying it could have been any of us; I want a doha that does that for everybody
Kabir called the careless to wake up before death put its hand on them, so write a doha in his urgent voice telling the reader to open his eyes this moment because the hour is nearly spent
doha that warns people to wake up right now before death takes them
Rise, you who sleep! The hour of leaving is nearer than the hour of waking
doha with a heron, wake up before its too late
The heron stands still and the water-dwellers watch it, and death stands still too: wake, wake, before it strikes
Write an urgent doha in which a heron stands patient at the water's edge while the sleepers below do not stir, telling all who sleep to wake because death waits as still as a heron
A heron stood in our pond for an hour, perfectly still, and nobody noticed until it struck; I thought of death, which stands as still as that, and I want a doha that wakes the sleepers
heron, wake up now
Sand falls through the glass of days and the sleeper sleeps on: wake, wake, for the last grain is falling
Write a doha in an urgent voice telling the heedless that the sand is running out in the glass of their lives, that death is the last grain, and that they must wake and act before it falls
My uncle had a sand clock on his desk, and last year after his heart attack he said now I see how fast it falls; I want a doha that wakes people before their last grain
sand, wake up now
doha with sand, wake up before the last grain falls
Write a doha in an urgent voice in which a moneylender counts his coins under a tree while death stands behind it, and the voice shouts at him to wake from his greed and do something that matters
moneylender, tree, wake up
doha with a moneylender and a tree, wake up before death comes
Under the tree the moneylender counts his coins, and death counts his breaths: wake, O fool, before the count is done
The moneylender who sat under the tree in our village counted coins until the day he died, and the coins stayed under the tree; I want a doha that shakes the next moneylender awake
At the funeral of my school friend, I stood there thinking that I'm next in some years, and that I've been dozing through everything; I want a doha that wakes up all the other dozing people
Write an urgent doha telling all who sleep in comfort that death is closer than they think, the call to wake has sounded for years, and today is the last day to answer
doha that tells everyone to wake up before death comes, loud and urgent
The sleeper dreams of a long road, and death is on the threshold: wake, wake, there is no time
wake up, now
The bee gathers honey under the stars and you are asleep: wake, O drowsy one, before the night of death
bee, stars, wake up
doha with a bee and stars, wake up before death comes
Write an urgent doha in which a bee works through the night under the stars while a person sleeps, telling him to wake and work before death ends the season of work
I watched a bee keep working under the stars as I lay on my cot, and then I got a call that my uncle had died; I want a doha that wakes me up and everyone like me
The cuckoo cries and the moneylender sleeps on his coins, and death sits on the bed: wake, wake
cuckoo, moneylender, wake up
Write an urgent doha in which a cuckoo calls while a moneylender sleeps on his coins, telling him to wake because death has come to take him from them
My neighbour the moneylender slept soundly on his money while a cuckoo called outside his window every morning, and then he was gone; I want a doha that wakes people like him
doha with a cuckoo and a moneylender, wake up before death comes
When the call came about my uncle's accident, I was in the middle of an argument about a tiny thing, and I felt my tongue freeze; I want a doha that wakes people from such petty sleep
The tongue is busy with idle talk, and death is busy at the threshold: wake, O sleeper, speak the true word now
tongue, wake up now
Write a doha in an urgent voice that tells the sleeper to use his tongue for the Name instead of idle talk, because death will soon still it for ever and the time for the Name will be gone
doha with a tongue, wake up before death shuts it
A parrot nearby keeps calling the old man's name, but he has been dead a week, and I felt it call me too; I want a doha that wakes up the sleepers
parrot, wake up
doha with a parrot, wake up before death comes
The parrot repeats the master's name in the empty rooms, and the voice cries: wake, wake, while the name is still yours
Write a doha in an urgent voice in which a parrot repeats borrowed words while its owner sleeps, and the voice tells him to wake and speak his own truth before death silences him
The skeleton in the field grins at the sleeper: wake, for you too will be bare, and soon
At the museum I stood beside a skeleton and suddenly could not breathe, thinking about my wasted years; I want a doha that gives everybody that jolt
Write a doha in an urgent voice in which a skeleton speaks to the sleeper, saying that it too slept once, that it too thought there was time, and that the sleeper must wake now before he joins it
doha with a skeleton, wake up before you end up like it
skeleton, wake up now
Write an urgent doha in which a river flows on while a person sleeps on the bank, telling him to wake and cross before death carries him away and the chance is lost
doha with a river, wake up before death comes
My uncle slept on the riverbank every afternoon for years, and the river rose one night and took everything; I want a doha for people who nap in the path of something bigger
river, wake up now
The river runs on while you sleep on its bank, and death is the flood that wakes no one: rise, rise now
